title: RE Robert Jamison v. Western Carolina Presbytery
disposition_detail: On the specification of error, the adjudicating commission voted 13-0 with one abstention not to sustain it and further voted to confirm the Western Carolina Presbytery's decision. It held the Presbytery's action in the discipline of TE "X" was in accordance with BCO 30-3, 4 and 34-7, citing BCO 34(7), the Fifth General Assembly declaration (M5GA p. 68), Presbytery's restorative purpose, and evidence of repentance. The Assembly was advised that Presbytery later denied TE "X's" request to demit and deposed him on June 6.
first_summary: Ruling Elder Robert Jamison complained that Western Carolina Presbytery failed to depose a Teaching Elder who had confessed to practicing bisexuality, instead suspending him indefinitely. The Judicial Commission denied the complaint and affirmed the Presbytery's decision, finding the Presbytery followed BCO 30-3, 4 and 34-7. The Commission reviewed only the constitutionality of the process, not the merits, and noted Presbytery's restorative purpose. Presbytery later deposed the Teaching Elder.
summary: A ruling elder complained that Western Carolina Presbytery wrongly left a confessing bisexual Teaching Elder under indefinite suspension rather than deposing him, excluding him from the sacraments, and cutting him off from fellowship. The General Assembly's adjudicating commission did not sustain the specification of error and confirmed Presbytery's action, holding it complied with BCO 30-3, 4 and 34-7. Review was limited to the constitutionality of the disciplinary process; the commission cited Presbytery's restorative purpose and evidence of repentance. The Assembly was advised Presbytery later deposed the Teaching Elder.

benchmark_examples: C01 (Allin): preserve both granted and refused relief; here relief was wholly refused because the complaint was not sustained and the lower court was affirmed.
C20 (Daniels): if a disposition is unexplained, do not supply reasons; here the adopted explanatory statement gives reasons, so they are reported.
